candidates.fit: tvs: unidirectional, VRWM 5V/VBR 6.4V min/Vc 9.2V@43.5A(10/1000us), 400W, huge stock+cheap; the industry-standard VBUS TVS choice, but Vc exceeds the 6V downstream abs-max under a real surge (see risks).

tvs: same electricals as SMAJ5.0A (5V/6.4V/9.2V) in a much smaller SOD-123 footprint, cheapest option; lower surge-power rating (200W@10/1000us vs 400W) - adequate given this board has no external cabling beyond a compliant USB-C cord.
tvs: same 5V/6.4V/9.2V electricals as SMAJ5.0A with more surge headroom (600W), bigger SMB footprint - pick if board area allows and extra surge margin is wanted over SMAJ5.0A.

tvs: Nexperia low-cap ESD-array-class part, VRWM 5V/VBR 7.5V/Vc 10V@4A(8/20us); MPN 'U' infix suggests unidirectional but polarity must be confirmed against the datasheet before use - lower surge-energy rating than the SM*J/SMF families, better suited to ESD duty than sustained power-line surge.

tvs: unidirectional (datasheet description confirms), 5V/7V standoff-breakdown, SOT-23 alternate package; lower stock than the SMA/SOD-123 picks - single-source-style risk if this exact reel runs out.

ptc: Ihold 750mA / Itrip 1.5A / Vmax 16V / Ri(initial) 90mOhm. 750mA is 2.14x the ~350mA worst-case load, clearing both the 1.2-1.5x margin rule and the ~0.75 hot-derating rule (350/0.75=467mA floor) with room to spare; 1206 is a common, well-stocked package.

ptc: same 750mA hold / 16V rating as the 1206 pick but smaller 0805 footprint and lower Ri (70mOhm, less LDO headroom eaten) and deeper stock; pick this over the 1206 if board area or dropout margin is tight.

ptc: Ihold 1A / Itrip 1.8A / Vmax 16V / Ri 55mOhm - lowest resistance and cheapest/highest-stock of the 16V family, but 1A hold is 2.86x worst-case load, so a partial fault in the 350mA-1A range would never trip; trade sensitivity for headroom and stock depth.

ptc: Ihold 500mA / Itrip 1A / Vmax 16V / Ri 150mOhm - cheapest PTC found and meets the literal >=0.5A hold floor, but 500/350=1.43x margin is thinner than the 750mA picks per the 1.2-1.5x design-margin rule; higher Ri also eats more LDO dropout budget.
ptc: same 500mA/16V/150mOhm electricals as the 0805 JK part in a 1206 footprint - alternate-package/alternate-vendor sourcing if the 0805 part is unavailable.

reverse: JLC Basic Schottky, 3A/40V rated (Vf 550mV@3A, well under that at the board's ~350mA), single-part series reverse-polarity block if the architect wants one - simplest option, no gate-drive support parts needed.

reverse: JLC Basic Schottky, 1A/40V (Vf 550mV@1A), cheapest series-diode option; same package as SS34 for negligible cost delta, SS34's extra current headroom is preferred unless BOM cost is the tiebreaker.
reverse: JLC Basic Schottky, 1A/40V, smaller SOD-123 footprint than SS14/SS34 if board area is the priority over current headroom.

reverse: JLC Basic P-channel MOSFET (30V/4A, Rds 47-85mOhm) for an ideal-diode/eFuse reverse-block - near-zero drop (~16mV@350mA vs ~0.35-0.55V for a Schottky) but needs 1-2 support passives (gate pull-down, optional gate-source clamp) and correct body-diode orientation; more design/validation burden than a plain Schottky for a low-value protection feature on this board. Note: this Basic-tagged listing prices higher per unit ($0.0968) than non-Basic dupes of the same MPN (~$0.037) - the Extended-part fee tradeoff should be checked by the part-sourcer at BOM time.
reverse: alternate JLC Basic P-channel MOSFET (20V/2.2-3.1A, Rds 110-142mOhm) if AO3401A stock/price is unfavorable at BOM time; 20V rating still clears the 5.5V VBUS max with margin.
